name: Lupus erythematosus tumidus

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: No standardized formal criteria; diagnosis based on clinical and histopathological features

criteria.description: Presence of erythematous, edematous, urticarial-like plaques without surface scale
Superficial and deep perivascular and periadnexal lymphocytic infiltrate with abundant dermal mucin deposition
Negative or weak/focal granular deposition of immunoglobulins and complement at the dermoepidermal junction
Lack of epidermal atrophy or follicular plugging differentiating from discoid lupus erythematosus

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Typical clinical lesions plus compatible histopathology findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other cutaneous lupus subtypes and photosensitive dermatoses

searchTerms: inflammation around deep skin blood vessels

laboratory: Normal complete blood count and metabolic panel
imaging: Not routinely indicated; skin biopsy is diagnostic
other: Skin biopsy showing perivascular and periadnexal lymphocytic infiltrate with abundant dermal mucin
Direct immunofluorescence typically negative or weak

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of epidermal atrophy and follicular plugging
Positive direct immunofluorescence with granular deposits
Transient papules and plaques resolving without scarring
Lack of dermal mucin on biopsy

redFlags: Rapid progression of skin lesions with ulceration
Development of systemic lupus erythematosus symptoms
Signs of secondary infection in skin lesions
references: Kuhn A, et al. Lupus erythematosus tumidus: clinical and histopathological features. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2010.
Werth VP. Cutaneous lupus erythematosus: clinical features and diagnosis. UpToDate. 2023.
Marzano AV, et al. Tumid lupus erythematosus: a distinct subset of cutaneous lupus erythematosus. Dermatol Clin. 2013.
